seo_title: Cost of Living in Ho Chi Minh City 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Ho Chi Minh City per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: Vietnam's economic hub and the country's largest metropolis: international offices, a lively startup scene and an affordable standard of living. A good fit for those who want to work in Asia without the resort format.
pros: Well-developed international infrastructure and a large expat zone
The lowest prices among the region's capitals
An English-speaking environment in Districts 1 and 2
An active startup scene and dozens of coworkings
Direct flights to every Asian capital
cons: A hot, humid climate with no seasons
A complicated visa for long-term stays

best_places.name: District 1
best_places.description: The business centre with skyscrapers, restaurants and the rooftop bar at Bitexco.

best_places.name: Thao Dien (District 2)
best_places.description: The main expat district with international schools, spas, restaurants and condominiums.

best_places.name: Toong Coworking
best_places.description: Vietnam's leading coworking chain, with meeting rooms and an active community of founders.

best_places.name: Ben Thanh Market
best_places.description: The city's central market: spices, textiles, street food and souvenirs — a starting point for tourists.

visa_steps.title: E-Visa
visa_steps.description: An electronic 90-day visa for Russian citizens, issued online in 3 days.

visa_steps.title: DN business visa
visa_steps.description: Via an invitation from a Vietnamese company. Up to 1 year with renewal.

visa_steps.title: Tax code (MST)
visa_steps.description: Needed for long-term rentals and for working with local employers.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Vietcombank, Techcombank and ACB open accounts with a DN visa and a rental contract.

visa_steps.title: Long-term rental
visa_steps.description: Contracts from 6 months with police registration. Prices are higher in Districts 1-2 and lower in District 7 and Phu Nhuan.

faq.question: How does Ho Chi Minh City differ from Da Nang?
faq.answer: Ho Chi Minh City is a business metropolis, Da Nang is a resort town. Ho Chi Minh City has more international work and infrastructure, but also more noise.

faq.question: Where should I live in Ho Chi Minh City?
faq.answer: Thao Dien (D2) — expats, schools, quiet. District 1 — the centre and work. District 7 — modern developments for families.

faq.question: How is English in Ho Chi Minh City?
faq.answer: In Districts 1 and 2 English is everywhere. In other districts Google Translate and basic Vietnamese help.

faq.question: How is banking in Ho Chi Minh City?
faq.answer: It's harder for Russians, but Vietcombank and ACB open accounts with a DN visa. SWIFT transfers work.

faq.question: What schools are there in Ho Chi Minh City?
faq.answer: International School Ho Chi Minh, BIS, Renaissance, AIS — from $18,000 a year.

faq.question: How is the internet in Ho Chi Minh City?
faq.answer: Fibre at 200+ Mbps for 700-1,000 ₽, plus 4G/5G mobile — excellent for remote work.

reviews.text: I moved my family to Thao Dien: a house for $1,200 with a pool, my daughter at BIS. I work for a Singapore bank and pay taxes in Russia. The downside is the long summer and the traffic jams.
I rented a studio in District 1 for $500 and work remotely. The city is lively and the cafés and street food are superb. The downside is that getting around is hard without a motorbike.
